title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Q is the combinatorial 'square' (vertices s, sides a) attached in these notes to an elliptic curve in characteristic ≠ 2. D = Aut Q is the dihedral group of order 8. The previous page fixed orientation conventions for the relation ϖcd = 1 and for the dual square Q°.

This page studies D as an abstract group.
- The centre Z = {1, ε} ≅ F2 equals the commutator subgroup.
- So D is a central extension 1 → F2 → D → D_ab = W → 1, with W ≅ F2×F2 (not canonically).
- W has a distinguished nonzero element ϖ: the image of the two elements of order 4, i.e. of the cyclic subgroup C4.
- The other two nonzero elements of W are the images of the two Klein four-subgroups:
  - V_S, symmetries through the vertices (diagonals), with C = V_S \ {1, ε};
  - V_A, symmetries through the sides, with D = V_A \ {1, ε}.
- An outer automorphism exchanges these two elements.

The automorphism group. This gives 1 → W̌ → Aut D → {±1} → 1.
- W̌ = Hom(W, F2) is the group of automorphisms of the extension that are the identity on F2 and on W.
- Such automorphisms are g ↦ g·φ(ḡ) with φ ∈ Hom(W, Z).
- The note (NB) says W̌ ≅ W canonically because W has rank 2 over F2. Precisely: a 2-dimensional F2-space carries a unique nondegenerate alternating form, which is also the commutator pairing of D.
- So Aut D ≅ W̌ ⋊ {±1}, with ±1 swapping the two non-distinguished elements. In particular Aut(D4) ≅ D4, of order 8.

Moduli meaning. For D coming from a curve, the choice of c (equivalently of C) versus d (equivalently of D) is extra structure. The automorphisms respecting it form W̌ ≅ W. These are exactly the inner automorphisms, Inn D ≅ D/Z ≅ W, since int: D → Aut D has kernel the centre.

Purpose. This prepares the next page's torsor description.
- A varying 'D' amounts to an F2²-torsor, i.e. the two two-element sets C and D.
- A varying Q amounts to a D4-torsor.
- The next page also remarks that Aut(D4) ≅ D4 non-innerly, suggesting a hypothetical equivalence (squares/'corps') → (groups ≅ D4) other than Q ↦ Aut Q. All of this serves to describe the level/rigidification data attached to elliptic curves with 2-power torsion structure in char ≠ 2.
errors: No mathematical error. The NB's 'canonical because rank 2' needs the justification that a rank-2 F2-space has a unique nondegenerate alternating (determinant) form; equivalently, use the commutator pairing of D.
Minor slip of notation: D denotes both the group Aut Q and the two-element set V_A \ {1, ε}.

ideas.what: D4 as a central extension of F2² by F2 with commutator subgroup = centre; distinguished element of D_ab coming from C4
ideas.modern_name: extraspecial/central extension structure of the dihedral group of order 8

ideas.what: Aut(D4) ≅ Hom(W, F2) ⋊ Z/2 ≅ D4, with Inn = automorphisms of the extension trivial on quotient and kernel
ideas.modern_name: automorphisms of central extensions = Hom(W, Z); Aut(D4) ≅ D4, Out(D4) = Z/2

ideas.what: Canonical identification W ≅ Hom(W, F2) for rank-2 F2-spaces via the alternating/commutator pairing
ideas.modern_name: Weil-pairing-type self-duality of a 2-dimensional symplectic F2-space

ideas.what: Interpretation of the two Klein subgroups (vertex vs side symmetries) as the data C, D attached to an elliptic curve; structure-preserving automorphisms = inner automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: level structures / torsors under D4 and its abelianization in moduli of elliptic curves

deep.surprise_reason: Routine finite group theory (the structure of Aut(D4)) set up to interpret moduli data as torsors. The slightly suggestive remark about a non-obvious equivalence via Aut(D4) ≅ D4 is on the next page and is speculative.
transcription_corrections: 'un élément non nul distingué, [...] inverse[?] de l'un ϖ' — the sense is 'image de l'un ϖ_(e) des deux éléments d'ordre 4 de D' (the distinguished element is the image of an element of order 4).
Marginal note reads: 'NB on a en fait un iso. can. W̌ ≃ W (W̌ à valeurs dans F2), car W de rg 2 sur F2'.
Label under W̌: 'autom. de D (ext. de W par F2) qui induisent l'identité sur W et F2'.
Bottom line: 'D = Aut Q', not 'D = Aut_Q'. The crossed-out formula is roughly 'D = F2 ×_{F2} F2' with labels C and D over the factors.
